archetypes.name: driver-contracts
archetypes.rationale: The plan moves routing responsibilities into shell drivers where stdout/KV and exit-code contracts are easy to drift.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit whether the proposed driver changes preserve the phase-driver result-env contract, clean stdout KV stream, and the intended exit-code semantics for cancel, resume, and init failure paths. Compare the plan against existing driver helpers and call sites to find missing argv threading, unsafe result-env parsing assumptions, or cases where rendering could pollute stdout or bypass required emits. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-retargeting
archetypes.rationale: Most acceptance criteria depend on relocating existing structural pins without deleting coverage or pinning the wrong surface.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review whether the testing plan fully retargets existing structure and router harness assertions from SKILL.md to the new driver-owned surfaces without losing behavioral coverage. Look for stale grep targets, missing pins for moved banners, insufficient assertions around stdout redirection and quiet-channel usage, and scope files that should be checked for doc drift but are absent. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: operator-channels
archetypes.rationale: The change is primarily about who emits operator-visible messages, so stderr/stdout and quiet-mode UX need focused scrutiny.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate the proposed operator-message flow across quiet mode, final-summary emission, cancel banners, and resume/init failure diagnostics. Check whether the plan risks duplicated, hidden, or misordered user-visible output when rendering moves from the orchestrator fence into drivers, especially around larch_err usage and final-summary.md verbatim emission. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
